title: A full walk run finishes in an hour, not four
goal: Running the whole set of scripted walks takes about four hours, and proving it repeats takes eight. That is long enough that nobody runs it before a change lands, so breaks are found days later by someone else. Make the set fast enough to run whenever it matters.
notes: Measured 2026-09-06: 188 walks, roughly 75 seconds each. Most of it is per-walk overhead rather than the walk. Every walk quits and relaunches the whole app (Scripts/probe-app.sh), and each launch also compiles and runs Scripts/permcheck.swift for the Grants line and polls up to 3s for dist/probe-grants.json. Candidates, cheapest first: cache the permcheck answer for the run; skip the grants poll when a previous launch already answered; drop the per-walk quit-relaunch by teaching the probe to take a second --playtest script without restarting, which is the big one. Watch out: walks currently rely on a fresh process for their starting state, and the harness now restores remembered settings at the end of every run, so a shared process would need that restore to happen between scripts too.
acceptance: Scripts/playtest-all.sh finishes in under an hour on this machine
The run prints how long it took, so the number stops being a guess
